angle: Sisay's currency is not cards or mana but ACCESS, and access is bought one colour at a time — 3, 10, 23, 28, 33 legal fetches at zero through four colours, with the whole jump living between the first colour and the second; the issue's proof piece is a checker that takes a famous 'two-card infinite' apart and hands back something more useful, a real unbounded combat loop that costs zero life and counts your mana base as its third member.

The Short List: ten cards, one five-pip bill, and the question asked of every pick

departments.headline: THE FIVE-COLOUR TECHNICALITY
departments.dek: A {2}{W} creature hands you a five-colour deck, and the record is untroubled by it: colour identity reads every mana symbol on the card, and her activation carries all five. The Counselor takes it from the top.
departments.body:
Start with the zone itself. CR 903.4 builds a commander's colour identity from every mana symbol in its mana cost and its rules text, and Sisay's activation — {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — puts all five colours in hers. A {2}{W} card is your licence to sleeve ninety-nine cards in five colours. That is not a loophole. It is the rule working exactly as printed, and it is the whole reason this deck exists.

The zone's guarantee matters more here than in most decks, because the card it guarantees is a search engine rather than a threat. CR 903.8 gives you that access at a rising price: {2} more for every previous cast from the zone. Sisay runs 3, then 5, then 7, then 9 — the ladder beside this column. Note what the tax does not touch. Her power is recomputed from the battlefield, so a recast Sisay walks back onto a surviving board at full strength. Spot removal costs you the tax and a turn. A sweeper costs you the tax and every rung at once. Those are different injuries, and only the second one is worth insuring against.

The 21-damage clock, CR 903.10a, is on the record and rarely on the plan. At four colours she is a 6/6 and three connections is lethal in theory. In practice her power is a gate rather than a weapon: the deck's actual lethal output is the section called The Kill. Treat commander damage as a bonus the scoreboard occasionally pays.

Now the Coach's half of the page. Protect her; do not budget for recasting her. The simulation holds a protection effect by turn six in 79.8% of games — Shalai, Flowering of the White Tree, Plaza of Heroes' exile mode, and two free instants. A recast costs you more than mana. It costs an activation window at a table that has already seen what she does.

And the political read is fixed before your first land drop. A five-colour commander who tutors on activation gets filed as the archenemy in the pregame, and four Game Changers in the list confirm it out loud. You are not going to argue the table out of that label. You are going to schedule when you deserve it.

captions.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: **GUARANTEED ACCESS:** the one card you always have is the one that goes and gets the rest. The 99 is built so that what she finds matters more than what you draw.

pilot_tips.text: Spend Plaza's last job on the turn that matters: {3}, tap, exile it, and a legendary creature has hexproof and indestructible through the wrath you can see coming.

departments.pull_quote: A {2}{W} card, a five-colour licence — the rule working exactly as printed.

departments.headline: COUNT COLOURS, NOT CARDS
departments.dek: Good Sisay pilots pass with all five pips available and no activation, and it looks like a misplay. The number that decides what she can find is not printed on her card — it is the count of distinct colours sitting beside her.

callouts.title: LAND HER, THEN WAIT
callouts.text: She costs {2}{W} and hits the battlefield on turn three in 8,028 of 10,000 seeded games. On arrival she is a 2/2 and the gate reads 'mana value less than 2' — three legal fetches in the entire deck, and no legendary lands sitting under it. Casting her was never the assignment.

callouts.title: BUY RUNGS ON FAIR BODIES
callouts.text: Every colour among your OTHER legendary permanents is +1/+1 on her and a wider gate. Katilda, Kinnan, Lotho and Saffi each carry two colours for two mana. Derevi carries three on one three-drop. None of them looks like a threat, and all of them are.

callouts.title: THE FIRST-TO-SECOND STEP IS THE GAME
callouts.text: The ladder runs 3, 10, 23, 28, 33 legal targets at zero through four colours. One colour to two adds THIRTEEN — the biggest jump on the ladder, and the step that first makes Najeela legal at mana value 3. Two to three adds only five. Buy the second colour early and buy it cheap.

callouts.title: STOP CLIMBING AT FOUR
callouts.text: Four colours already unlocks all 33, because nothing in this deck costs more than five. The fifth colour buys combat stats and Jodah's anthem and exactly zero new access. That is a false pivot — spend the turn holding protection instead.

callouts.title: COUNT THE BILL IN PIPS
callouts.text: {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, zero generic, every activation. Six cards can carry most of it alone: Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, Relic of Legends, Selvala. The simulation puts Sisay beside one of them by turn six 55.8% of the time. Count coloured sources, never total mana.

pilot_tips.text: Cast it, love it, and never count it toward an activation — {C}{C} pays zero of her five pips.

captions.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: **THE SCOREBOARD:** +1/+1 for each colour among your other legendary permanents, and a gate of 'mana value less than her power'. Her stat line is a live count of how much of your library is legal.
captions.Katilda, Dawnhart Prime: **THIRTEEN CARDS FOR TWO MANA:** white and green on one two-drop takes you from one colour to two, and the fetch pool from 10 legal targets to 23. Nothing else in the deck moves the number that far that cheaply.
captions.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: **THREE RUNGS, ONE CARD:** white, blue and green at mana value 3. She alone takes Sisay from a 2/2 to a 5/5 and the fetch pool from 3 targets to 28.

departments.pull_quote: One colour is ten cards. Two colours is twenty-three. Buy the second one early, and buy it on something nobody fears.

departments.headline: EVERY LEGEND EARNS ITS SEAT
departments.dek: Fifty-nine spells, one question each: does it climb the ladder, pay the bill, or hold the window open? The roster is ranked by load — the six cards that can actually pay her lead, and the lands report to Sources Say.

roster.role: The pip battery — the only six that can pay her
cards: Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic Bridge

The ladder — colours on fair bodies
cards: Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolarian Obliterator

Acceleration — and what it cannot buy

captions.Bloom Tender: **THE BEST CARD SHE CAN'T FIND:** one mana of each colour among permanents you control, compounding with the very colours the ladder counts — and non-legendary, so it arrives by draw or not at all.
captions.Loran of the Third Path: **THE EXCEPTION:** the deck's only artifact-and-enchantment answer on a legendary body, which makes her the only answer in the 99 Sisay can go and get.

pilot_tips.text: Do not build a cold-start plan on fetching Mikaeus — {X}{W} put onto the battlefield rather than cast may mean X is zero, and that question is still open on the record.

departments.note: Lands fall deliberately into the Depth group; the mana base gets its own audit in Sources Say. Roster group names feed the Featured Artist overlap table — keep them short and stable.

departments.headline: MULLIGAN FOR ENABLERS
departments.dek: In a deck whose payoffs fetch themselves, the keep is never about payoffs. The Coach wants fuel and a cheap legend; Ledger's ten thousand hands keep 84.2% of first sevens on the land rule alone — so the judgement was never about lands either.

hands.why: Unrestricted colour, the best battery piece in the deck, and two bodies carrying five rungs between them. Sisay arrives on curve and the ladder is at three colours by turn five. This is the enabler hand the whole section is asking for.
Five payoffs, two lands, no fixing. Every legend here is a fetch target — the hand is full of cards Sisay could have found for free, and empty of the fuel she never will.

The trap keep. It curves out beautifully and pays nothing: Sol Ring is colourless, the Halfling's coloured mana is legendary-spells-only, the Territory is creature-spells-only. She lands a turn early and stares at a five-pip bill this hand cannot cover.
Three lands with real colour, a rock that pays any pip, a two-rung legend and one answer to hold. Not flashy — exactly the shape that 84.2% keep rate is made of.

pilot_tips.text: Treat one untapped Bird as the difference between keep and ship — an early accelerant shows up by turn six in only 63.8% of games, so a hand holding one is already ahead of the deck's own curve.

captions.Delighted Halfling: **THE FALSE FRIEND:** she ramps Sisay out a turn early and makes her uncounterable, then pays not one pip of what Sisay does next. A cast-turn card, never an activation-turn card.

departments.headline: COMMIT BEFORE YOU PEEK
departments.dek: Two real boards from this deck's midgame: a Dimir seat holding four cards, and a pod that has just watched your first fetch resolve. Pick your line at each fork — the Coach's call is printed after the branches, never before.

pilot_tips.text: Hold it for the activation you intend to convert, not the first one you can afford — one white mana buys the whole turn.

departments.pull_quote: Every activation is public. The decision behind it doesn't have to be.

departments.headline: PARTIALLY ACCURATE, WHOLLY LETHAL
departments.dek: The combo database pleads Najeela plus Derevi as a two-card infinite. Twenty-four steps and three review cycles later the record says something better and stranger: a genuine, deterministic, unbounded combat loop that kills for zero life — once you can raise the first five pips yourself.

callouts.title: PRE-FUND COMBAT ONE
callouts.text: Two attackers declared, one Warrior token, three attackers connecting and three Derevi triggers — two short of the five-mana activation. Combat one is paid by the five untapped lands you kept back before combat. Budget for it or the loop never starts.

callouts.title: BREAK EVEN ON COMBAT TWO
callouts.text: Five creatures connect, five triggers, five pips. Exactly even, and self-sustaining from here: tap, pass priority, let a Derevi trigger untap the land, tap it again — all inside one damage step.

callouts.title: RUN AWAY ON COMBAT THREE
callouts.text: Attackers follow 2A−1: three, five, nine, seventeen, thirty-three. Triggers equal attackers while the cost stays fixed at five, so the margin only widens. Damage runs 6, 8, 12, 20 — the first defending player dies as a state-based action during combat four's damage.

callouts.title: THE ARMY STAYS
callouts.text: A defending player leaving the game is not on CR 506.4's list of ways to leave combat, so all seventeen attackers remain attacking. Commander's default attack-multiple-players option makes every opponent a defending player, so combat five redirects the whole army at the next seat.

callouts.title: THE FLOOR IS ZERO LIFE
callouts.text: Both triggers say 'you may', so you iterate by choice and shortcut to lethal. Command Tower and Plaza of Heroes cover all five colours between them, and activating a mana ability is never mandatory — City of Brass and Mana Confluence never have to be tapped at all.

captions.Najeela, the Blade-Blossom: **THE LOUD HALF:** every Warrior that attacks makes another Warrior, and her five-pip untap is the same bill Sisay charges. The pip battery double-duties as combo fuel.
captions.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: **THE QUIET HALF:** one untap trigger per creature connecting, not per damage event. Reads as a fair 2/3 right up to the combat where the triggers equal the bill.

pilot_tips.text: Fetch her on the turn she wins, not the turn she impresses — until then she is safer in your library than in your hand.

departments.pull_quote: Not a two-card infinite. A two-card engine with your mana base as its third member.

departments.headline: THE FOURTH-MOST-INTERESTING BOARD
departments.dek: A five-colour tutor deck gets left alone right up until the table can count five untapped colour sources beside her. Your whole midgame is a game about what the pod can see — and what it can't.

callouts.title: THE THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: You flip to archenemy when three things land together: three or more colours among your other legends, five pips genuinely payable, and protection up. That is also your pivot. If you are going to wear the label, cash it for the window rather than the applause.

callouts.title: THE TELLS, RANKED
callouts.text: A body that visibly solves the bill — Jegantha, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Esika — is louder than any legend you fetch. Najeela is louder still. A second activation inside one turn cycle ends the conversation.

callouts.title: HOW THE GOOD PILOTS KILL YOU
callouts.text: Not with removal on Sisay. They kill the rung — the one legend supplying a colour — in response to the activation, so her power drops and the fetch shrinks under you. Audit your single-sourced colours every turn and deploy the redundant one before the greedy fetch.

pilot_tips.text: Tap Loran while an opponent is deciding whether to attack you — the cheapest goodwill this deck buys is one shared card.

captions.Rhystic Study: **THE TELL YOU DIDN'T CHOOSE:** a Game Changer Sisay can never fetch, and the card most likely to make you archenemy before you have decided to be. At a table still choosing a target, sit on it a turn.
captions.Shalai, Voice of Plenty: **THE RETIREMENT PLAN:** hexproof for you and every other creature you control. One fetch ends the kill-the-rung attack — go and get her before you need her, not after.

departments.pull_quote: Play the whole midgame as a fair legends deck. You are never more than one activation from the truth.

departments.headline: FOUR WAYS YOU LOSE
departments.dek: Every pod holds a seat that beats you: a wrath, a lock, a swarm, a stack. Know which one you are facing, and which of your outs is real, before the ladder decides for you.

threats.read: They let you build, then take the board and the ladder with one card — a wrath drops you from 28 legal fetches back to 3. Commit exactly what wins and bank a two-colour legend in HAND: the hand copy rebuilds two rungs, the board copy dies with everything else. And know which of your saves actually saves; indestructible beats destruction and does nothing against exile or a -X/-X.

A five-pip activation with zero generic has nothing to pay around, which makes this the most tax-exposed shape in the format. You are the beatdown: race the lock's completion instead of out-valuing it, and recount your activations under the tax rather than your cards. Then name the piece locking YOU, not the scariest piece on the table.

You cannot race roughly 120 life behind three defences, and the simulation has you at four bodies on turn six — so stop trying. Buy virtual answers instead of spending real ones: their creatures arrive tapped, their draws cost life, your creatures get hexproof. One fetch that blanks plans at three seats beats one removal spell that answers one card.

The endgame collapses to a count of held interaction, and yours is exactly what Sisay cannot see: all six counterspells and both free protection instants are non-legendary. Invert the default — hold the pips up and count the table's open mana instead of climbing, because a wide gate is worth nothing if the game ends before you walk through it.

pilot_tips.text: You get to choose the wipe's timing, so choose the turn you rebuild cheapest — the ladder comes back faster than any board it takes down.

captions.Dauthi Voidwalker: **THE BLIND CLASS:** this deck answers creatures, artifacts and enchantments, and answers neither graveyards nor lands. Against a reanimator seat he is the answer — and he is non-legendary, so he arrives by draw.

departments.headline: FOUR WISHES, ONE CAPTAIN
departments.dek: Most decks get one wish per tutor card; yours reloads every time you can raise five pips. Four scenarios cover the whole game — the default, the rebuild, the closer and the one nobody sees coming — plus the 26 cards she will never find, so you can stop wishing for them.

pilot_tips.text: Know your second choice before you announce the first — the power check happens on resolution, so a rung killed in response can leave you choosing from a shorter list than you planned.

captions.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: **THE FUEL SHE CAN FIND:** half the pip battery is invisible to her. Selvala is legendary at mana value 3, so she is legal from the second colour onward — and one tap off a big enough creature is the whole {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}.
captions.Teferi, Time Raveler: **THE FETCH NOBODY EXPECTS:** three mana, legal from the second colour, and opponents are cut to sorcery speed for the rest of the game. Some wishes are for cards that end games; this one is for a turn where nothing can go wrong.

departments.pull_quote: Fetch only what she alone can reach. Draw the rest, and stop resenting it.

departments.headline: FIVE PIPS, ZERO GENERIC
departments.dek: Forty lands, and not one generic symbol in the bill they pay. Flat sources under very unflat pips is the whole story: this base is priced for the activation rather than the cast costs, and the audit zeroes every restricted source before it counts a single one.

pilot_tips.text: Name Human. 'Or activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type' is the clause that lets this land pay Sisay's activation — and Sisay is a Human Soldier. Unclaimed Territory's text never will.

captions.Plaza of Heroes: **READ THE CLAUSE, NOT THE PHRASE:** the legendary-spell mode cannot pay an activated ability. The third mode — any colour among legendary permanents you control — pays her fine. One land, four different answers.
captions.Sheoldred, the Apocalypse: **WHY BLACK CARRIES ITS OWN TARGET:** black is the one colour where the cards want two pips rather than one, so its source target sizes for two black sources by turn three. Twelve black lands gets there on curve 29.9% of the time; the dorks and rocks drag it to 61.0%.

departments.headline: SHE WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded games put Sisay on the battlefield by turn six 99.1% of the time — so why does the deck feel slow? Because the real curve is the assembly, and commander plus a five-colour source lands by turn six only 55.8% of the time.

callouts.title: TURN THREE, LIKE CLOCKWORK
callouts.text: Mean cast turn 2.963, median 3, 99.1% by turn six — and 8,028 of 10,000 games cast her exactly on turn three. Casting the commander is the one promise this deck always keeps, which is why you never mulligan for it.

callouts.title: THE ASSEMBLY IS THE CURVE
callouts.text: Sisay beside a multi-colour mana body: assembled in 67.9% of games, 55.8% by turn six, mean turn 4.219. The gap between 'commander out' and 'engine online' is where your mulligans and your first two fetches live.

callouts.title: MANA CROSSES FIVE AT TURN SIX
callouts.text: Mean available mana runs 3.187 on turn three, 4.063 on turn four and 5.869 on turn six. A five-pip activation is barely affordable on curve even before you ask about colours — which is precisely why a battery body is not optional.

callouts.title: PROTECTION IS ALREADY THERE
callouts.text: A protection effect is available by turn six in 79.8% of games, at a mean turn of 2.3. Stop sandbagging a save you probably already hold and fetch into that number instead.

departments.pull_quote: The commander arrives on schedule in every simulation. The engine is the part you build.

departments.headline: JUDGED AGAINST ONE BILL
departments.dek: One cost governs this deck — {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, no generic to pay around — and every card here was asked the same question. Six buy a second payment of it. The other four close the permanent class the 99 cannot answer, add a finisher the count can see, and put a second, structurally different kill on the table.
departments.pull_quote: The bracket column is flat: 4 before and 4 after, on all ten. Nothing here is a power-level decision wearing an upgrade's coat.
departments.note: The renderer draws the ten from considering.json. Every combo line an entry opens is flagged 'needs a stack scenario' there — keep every one priced as a candidate, never as fact. WARNING for the orchestrator: manual_prose.json's `upgrades` key describes a different ten (Gaea's Cradle, Minamo, The One Ring, Captain Sisay, Kethis) and renders directly above this list. Ledger's prose needs re-running against the current considering.json before publication.

departments.headline: READ TWICE, STAMPED ONCE
departments.dek: One case carries this issue: A-002, the Najeela–Derevi loop. Twenty-four steps, every Comprehensive Rules citation quoted verbatim, three review cycles. The holding is 'partially accurate' — and that is exactly why you can trust the rest of this magazine.
departments.note: Only stack 002 carries checker.verdict == 'pass' and may render. The other two artifacts carry failing verdicts; their open questions are listed under gaps and are never cited as fact anywhere in the issue.

departments.headline: EIGHTY-ONE HANDS
departments.dek: Eighty-one artists across ninety-nine cards, and the leader holds exactly five. A gallery of one-ofs, which is the most singleton fact about a singleton deck.

featured.note:
Five cards of ninety-nine is what leading this roster looks like. Nobody else painted more than four, no product drop concentrated anyone's hand, and the counting here is per card — never per copy, which is the honest way to count a deck that runs basics.

Belledin's five are quietly load-bearing. Two of them are cards a cold-start Sisay can legally fetch at base power — Mox Amber and Mikaeus, the Lunarch — one is the deck's only fetchable artifact-and-enchantment answer in Loran of the Third Path, and the other two are Exotic Orchard and a Forest. Five cards, and three of them appear somewhere else in this issue as a rules problem.

The spread is the story rather than the leader. Eighty-one hands for ninety-nine cards means this deck was assembled one card at a time, and the credits are the proof.

also_worth_noting.note: Four entries, all lands — Hallowed Fountain, Overgrown Tomb, Steam Vents, Temple Garden. The shock-dual backbone the audit counts, in one hand.
Jegantha, the Wellspring and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse — the only card that pays the whole bill off one tap, and the heaviest hitter in the tax shell.
Flooded Strand and Windswept Heath — two of the nine fetchlands, and two of the choices where the audit says take black.
Esper Sentinel and Grand Abolisher — the white hatebears, both non-legendary, both arriving by draw.
Drannith Magistrate and Kenrith, the Returned King — a Game Changer she cannot see and a five-colour king she reaches only at power 6.
Boros Charm and Flawless Maneuver — two of the eight insurance cards, and the two that answer a destruction wrath rather than an exile one.

captions.Loran of the Third Path: **THE BELLEDIN PICK:** if one of his five decides a game, it is this one — the single answer in the deck Sisay can go and get.

departments.pull_quote: No drop, no block buy, no house style. Ninety-nine cards chosen one at a time, and the credits show it.

rhythm_notes: Canonical five-act order throughout, and The Kill closes Act II as the peak. The only legal dense adjacency — Sources Say (analysis) into By the Numbers (analysis) — is split by the declared full-bleed art break the renderer emits after Sources Say, so Sources Say deliberately carries no pull quote and lets the break do the breathing. Act III runs three straight Coach sections and Act IV three straight Ledger ones, so the register never whipsaws; the transitions inside each act are carried by furniture instead of voice. What's Your Play (participation) is buffered by Keep or Ship (practice) before it and Table Manners (reflection) after. Judge's Desk sits between The Kill's narrative and Featured Artist's appreciation and closes gently into the Back Page. Pull quotes ride The Command Zone, The Game Plan, What's Your Play, The Kill, Table Manners, Fetch Quests, By the Numbers, The Short List and Featured Artist as micro-breathers; Keep or Ship, Know Your Enemy and Sources Say run deliberately lean because each already carries meters or boxes.
gaps: PUBLICATION BLOCKER: manual_prose.json's `upgrades` key narrates a different ten from the one in considering.json — it discusses Gaea's Cradle, Minamo, The One Ring, Captain Sisay and Kethis, while the current list is Intruder Alarm, Cryptolith Rite, Bear Umbra, Marvin, Chromatic Lantern, Vito, Urborg, Beast Within, Freed from the Real and Walking Ballista. The renderer prints the prose immediately above the list, so the section currently contradicts itself. This plan's Short List copy follows considering.json; the prose key needs re-running.

Two stack artifacts carry a failing checker verdict, and between them sits the deck's highest-leverage open question: whether a legend fetched this turn can help pay for a second activation the same turn (Relic of Legends' second mode versus Esika's granted tap ability). Re-scope to one rules domain per scenario and resolve. Neither may be cited until it passes.

Mikaeus, the Lunarch fetched rather than cast — does no value chosen for X make him a 0/0? It decides whether the cold-start pool is three cards or two, and it is flagged as open in The 99's pilot tip and in Fetch Quests' notes.

Nine of the ten combo lines fully contained in this deck are unverified candidates: the three Najeela pairs, the four Emiel and Selvala blink loops, Ioreth–Samut–Selvala, and the five-card Jegantha line. Only case A-002 is stated as fact anywhere in this issue.

The Short List opens four more stack-worthy scenarios flagged 'needs a stack scenario' in considering.json: Bear Umbra plus Najeela, Marvin plus Ioreth, Intruder Alarm plus Sisay plus a mana body, and Walking Ballista plus Heliod. Vito plus Najeela is read off oracle text with no combo record at all and is the least-grounded line on the page.

Strategy DB holes named in the strategic frame, all of which this issue routes around rather than cites: toolbox and silver-bullet construction, access-as-a-resource, playing the stax seat proactively, removal-in-response as an attack on an ability's own gate, per-iteration toll on a loop finisher, five-colour mana pricing, and restricted mana that cannot pay an activated ability. Seven research topics for the strategy-researcher.
No deck recon exists for this commander, so nothing in the issue is weighed against what strong Sisay lists actually run.
